title: Invalid UTF-8 byte 0xaa in instance creation payload (TC-EE-10-06, TC-EXT-01-INT-07)
notes: Cluster K from Step 5c. 85 occurrences of POSTGRES ERROR C22021 'invalid byte sequence for encoding UTF8: 0xaa' at unnamed portal parameter $1 (mbutils.c:1665 report_invalid_encoding). The errors cluster inside two tests: TC-EE-10-06 (EXECUTION_ERROR payload contains all required fields, in tests/integration/instance_error_test.zig:852) and TC-EXT-01-INT-07 (exhausted retries move the failure to OBS-05 DLQ and ERROR, in tests/integration/ext01_service_task_test.zig, surfacing from src/engine/instance.zig:699 create). The failing call site is `const inst = try inst_store.create(allocator, def.id, null, "{\"foo\":\"bar\"}");` — null payload literal combined with a JSON string. Symptom in vendor/pg/pg.zig:303 readUntilReady: bytes 0xAA appear in the wire protocol because the JSON parameter is bound as a raw byte buffer rather than a UTF-8 validated string. Likely root cause: Zig 0.16.0 libpq binding parameter type inference regression, OR the test passes a stale null-marker byte from a previous failed transaction. Evidence: scratch/WF03-gh375-20260801/test-runner-step5c/zig_test_integration.log offsets 924607, 924787, 924967.

root_cause.details: After running WF03-gh388-20260802 Step 1 diagnosis (scratch/WF03-gh388-20260802/issue-fixer-step1/diagnosis.{md,yaml}), the 0xAA byte does NOT originate from a Zig-side buffer in src/engine/instance.zig or vendor/pg/pg.zig — all bind sources verified pure-ASCII. The 0xAA originates server-side inside the audit_entries.resource_id TEXT column (after GBL-081 widened it from UUID to TEXT). The BEFORE INSERT trigger bpm_audit_apply_chain_hash (migrations/051_xc02_audit_immutability.sql:30-90) calls bpm_audit_compute_chain_hash (migrations/035_adp09_tamper_evident_audit_chain.sql:88-130) whose signature still declares p_resource_id UUID. The implicit UUID cast or convert_to(..., 'UTF8') rejects when NEW.resource_id contains 0xAA, bubbles C22021 to the originating INSERT, which PG reports as the original bind parameter $1. The interleaved C23503/C42703/C23514 errors in the same log regions confirm shared-DB-state contamination (similar to ISS-0112 / GH #375). The audit chain hash trigger pipeline is the actual defect; the JSON '{"foo":"bar"}' payload is a red herring. Confidence: medium.

candidate_resolution: Migrate bpm_audit_compute_chain_hash to accept p_resource_id TEXT (drop implicit UUID cast), and update bpm_audit_chain_canonical_payload accordingly. Alternatively, in bpm_audit_apply_chain_hash, validate NEW.resource_id is valid UTF-8 before calling compute_chain_hash; if invalid, normalise to a placeholder so audit never blocks business writes. Add tests/integration/audit_chain_utf8_test.zig regression test that inserts a parent row with 0xAA in its primary-key TEXT column and asserts the chain hash trigger does NOT raise C22021.
prevention: Add a per-call UTF-8 validation step in the pool.zig exec helper so coding errors surface locally rather than as Postgres errors mid-pipeline.
Add a Zig-side smoke test that constructs and binds a JSON payload of multiple encodings and asserts the wire bytes are valid UTF-8.
